answer: Measure each identity's marginal contribution by holding it out: at every close, recompute the grades as if that key had never voted. An honest grader shifts outcomes in scattered, small ways. A sybil cluster shows a telltale delta, since removing any one member barely changes anything while its siblings carry the same votes. That redundancy is the signal: keys whose removal changes nothing earn close to nothing, so a farm's payout sinks toward its nadir no matter how many keys it adds. Real contribution stays visible and hard, like onyx under polishing.
